title: Gate 3 release authorization for a paired browser (owner-gated)
description:

Measurement in parent comment-4157b81a24544fab8ca45702d1843fd5 at b1da2cb9d88515dcfce1046d0cac0a0eaeed01de. This is NOT the missing contract-bound lane helper; that remains independently owned by task-6bafd3b9439640cba358dd6e79329c9d.

OBJECTIVE: resolve and enforce the exact browser identity allowed to spend release.decide without opening MCP, impersonating the configured operator, or changing evidence/admission/replay authority. This row is OWNER-GATED before any production authority change. Candidate for the owner's decision: a release-only authorization arm for a currently authenticated, project-bound durable HUMAN with ADMIN, retaining its own principal id; configured operator behavior remains unchanged. The candidate is NOT approved by the parent's preserve-scope ruling. The owner may instead require an explicit operator step-up design; if that requires a new command/wire, split its producer work before implementation under the epic rails.

OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS includes release and MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS derives from it at mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:94. Changing only the synchronous waiver does nothing; deleting the roster entry also opens MCP and is forbidden.

This production-registry arm confirms OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION. It does not claim a live browser pass.

DELIVERABLE after explicit owner approval: one focused release authorization policy composed at every reachable release entry, with positive/negative tests and unchanged command identity, evidence checks, durable receipts and MCP exclusion. Expected implementation envelope is <=8 named files, with production modules <=250 lines; pin exact files when policy is approved. No new command kind is assumed.

NOT IN SCOPE: completing the contract-goal harness, editing the browser proof to use configured credentials, replacing a click with direct operator dispatch, hand-seeding evidence, changing the operator/MCP roster, live PR creation, main integration, or unrelated gate widening. No source edits before the owner's specific ruling is recorded.

EXACT focused verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release`. Run fresh foreground, nonzero count lines required. The owning plan also names the existing MCP exclusion test and full daemon regression. Parent task-817d893f retains full live-browser acceptance and the existing epic-final task-6cbcf5ff retains whole-epic hardening; do not create a separate evidence row.
definitionOfDone: Before production edits, an owner-authored or explicitly attributed owner ruling in a row comment selects the exact release-only authorization instrument and resolves its compatibility with the epic's operator-only rail. The plan has an explicit STOP before authority-changing steps. If not approved, remain blocked; neither scope preservation nor SPEED auto-approval supplies this authorization.

The approved policy is composed at every reachable release admission layer, including the durable command wrapper, service and unconfigured branch where applicable. Authenticated actor identity remains the actual caller; no operator impersonation, browser credential injection or parallel authorization implementation. Existing configured-operator behavior is preserved.

Production-surface tests prove the approved browser principal reaches release admission while agent, unknown/non-current session, wrong-project and insufficient-capability principals refuse with exact code AND layer before dossier, publication or PR effects; assert zero side-effect calls on refused arms and include replay/actor-identity coverage.

release.decide remains in the operator/human-only classification and excluded from MCP, with bidirectional served/excluded roster assertions. No other command's authorization changes; tests include a non-release operator kind as a negative control.

Focused `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` and the plan's MCP/daemon gates run fresh foreground with nonzero test counts and exit statuses. Record one bounded mutation proving the chosen authorization predicate is load-bearing, prove exact restoration, and disclose path-attributed foreign failures rather than calling them green.
taskRails: OWNER APPROVAL IS A HARD STOP before production authorization edits. The parent's scope ruling is not a waiver of operator-only authority and does not choose this policy.
Do not remove release.decide from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS or alter derived MCP exclusions; do not substitute the configured operator credential/principal into browser requests.
The async release path bypasses the synchronous registry waiver. Trace and test the actual command wrapper plus service; no one-line sync waiver claimed as a fix.
Keep this a focused production authorization slice with its own tests. The parent owns end-to-end release proof and the existing epic-final owns full integration hardening.

implementationPlan.description: TEST FIRST (DoD 2-4). Build a test-tier harness using SqliteEventStore.openEphemeralForProjectTest, ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding, createDaemonCommandPorts and the REAL createSessionAuthenticator, following repository-bootstrap-authorization.test.ts. Use startControlRoomListener with the production createOperatorSessionHandshakePort; the positive browser identity must come from /session/pair/request -> listener.approvePairing -> /session/pair/claim, not a hand-written AuthenticatedPrincipal or configured operator credential. Construct a normal four-field release payload on a fresh release aggregate and send it through /command. Fully compose release's production handler with counting dossier/publisher/PR effect ports; deliberately leave the remote unbound so an authorized request reaches exact RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING @ PROJECT_REDUCER at DISPATCH, while current code instead fails OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION. Assert the paired id differs from operator, the durable command decision uses the paired id, and the operator key is absent. Add cases for HUMAN with GOAL but no ADMIN; ADMIN but no GOAL; a valid agent session with no durable HUMAN principal; unknown, exactly-expired and CLOSED credentials; cross-project credential use; direct command-boundary project mismatch; configured operator unchanged; authorized but unconfigured release; and a non-release operator command such as goal.close remaining denied to the same paired ADMIN. For session close/agent setup reuse session-test-fixtures.ts send/envelope/openPayload against runSessionCommand, with explicit fixture project/session overrides, rather than writing accepted authority rows. Bound each HTTP operation; close listener/store in finally/afterEach on success, refusal and thrown assertions. No bearer-bearing logs or snapshots. Run the narrow new spec to show the intended positive-authorization assertion RED before implementation; do not change the expected prerequisite refusal to today's operator refusal.

Unknown/unreadable principal data and failed durable reads must fail closed with the existing OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED / DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION / 403, never an unhandled exception or successful fallback. Authentication remains the separate production ingress check, not something this helper claims to perform; document the trust contract. Keep the existing project mismatch check, payload validation, command/base identity digest, expected-version admission, pending-command exclusion and actual-principal decision keys unchanged. Do not rewrite the principal, session credential, request bytes or replay identity. Keep this production file <=250 lines; its existing .js bridge already reexports the new internal symbol.

SHAPE. assertReleasePrincipal keeps the original two checks in their original order: the operator-identity refusal (OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED / DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION / 403), then the unchanged RELEASE_PROJECT_MISMATCH / 403. Because the project check still runs AFTER, a configured operator on a wrong project keeps RELEASE_PROJECT_MISMATCH exactly as before.

releaseByPairedAdmin returns true only for the conjunction of FOUR separately-enforced conditions: envelope.commandKind === KIND ("release.decide", the module's existing constant — the disjunct cannot leak to another kind); principal.projectId === options.projectId; principal.capabilities.includes(CAPABILITIES.ADMIN); and isDurableHumanPrincipal(options.store, principal.principalId). The owner's second trap is addressed head-on and documented in the header: isDurableHumanPrincipal proves ONLY durable-record-FOUND + kind HUMAN, so it establishes neither authentication nor project binding nor ADMIN, and each of those is checked in its own right. Authentication remains the separate production ingress check (authenticateHttpRequest) — the helper documents that trust contract rather than claiming to perform it. The capability check is deliberately redundant with the ingress capability gate: defence in depth, and it is the conjunct the step-7 mutation drill removes.
